friedlein:1873.author: Proclus Diadochus (ed. Gottfried Friedlein)
friedlein:1873.work: Procli Diadochi in primum Euclidis Elementorum librum commentarii
friedlein:1873.note: Standard critical Teubner Greek edition (pp. 1–436, Indices pp. 437–507; CTS URN urn:cts:greekLit:tlg4036.tlg011.opp-grc1) providing canonical page-and-line numbering.

taylor:1788.author: Thomas Taylor (trans.)
taylor:1788.work: The Philosophical and Mathematical Commentaries of Proclus, on the First Book of Euclid's Elements, Vol. I
taylor:1788.note: First English translation, Volume I covering Prologue Book I, Prologue Book II, and Definitions.

taylor:1789.author: Thomas Taylor (trans.)
taylor:1789.work: The Philosophical and Mathematical Commentaries of Proclus, on the First Book of Euclid's Elements, Vol. II
taylor:1789.note: First English translation, Volume II covering Petitions/Postulates, Axioms, and Propositions I.1–I.48.

grynaeus:1533.author: Simon Grynaeus (ed.)
grynaeus:1533.work: Εὐκλείδου Στοιχείων βιβλ. ιε΄ ... Procli in primum Euclidis Elementorum librum commentariorum libri IIII (Editio Princeps)
grynaeus:1533.note: Editio princeps of the Greek text of Euclid and Proclus's Commentary, whose pagination appears in the left margin of Friedlein and was used by Thomas Taylor.

barocius:1560.author: Franciscus Barocius (Francesco Barozzi)
barocius:1560.work: Procli Diadochi Lycii in primum Euclidis Elementorum librum commentariorum ad universam mathematicam disciplinam principium eruditionis tradentium libri IIII
barocius:1560.note: Renaissance Latin translation collated from superior Greek manuscripts in Venice and Crete, supplying crucial lacunae of the 1533 Basel Greek text.

plato:rep:VI.510b-511d.author: Plato
plato:rep:VI.510b-511d.note: Foundational Platonic text establishing dianoia and mathematical objects as intermediate (metaxy) between sensibles and pure intelligibles (Friedlein 3–4, 10, 42).

plato:rep:VII.525a-534e.author: Plato
plato:rep:VII.525a-534e.note: Mathematics as the 'prelude' awakening the eye of the soul and Dialectic as the 'coping-stone' (thrigkos) of the sciences (Friedlein 20–29, 42–44).

plato:timaeus:31c-36d.author: Plato
plato:timaeus:31c-36d.note: Harmonic composition of the World-Soul and construction of the five regular cosmic polyhedra—identified by Proclus as the ultimate skopos of Euclid's Elements (Friedlein 16, 62, 70–71).

plato:meno:81e-85d.author: Plato
plato:meno:81e-85d.note: Recollection (anamnesis) demonstrated by Socrates eliciting the doubling of the square from an untaught boy, proving mathematical logoi are innate in the soul (Friedlein 45).

plato:parmenides:137e.author: Plato
plato:parmenides:137e.note: Plato's optical definition of the straight line as 'that of which the middle covers both extremities' (Friedlein 109–110).

plato:philebus:16c-26d.author: Plato
plato:philebus:16c-26d.note: Metaphysics of Limit (peras) and the Unlimited (apeiron) as cosmic principles generating all mathematical harmony and figure (Friedlein 5–7).

aristotle:anal-post:I.1-10.author: Aristotle
aristotle:anal-post:I.1-10.note: Theory of apodictic science, first principles (axioms, hypotheses, postulates), and universal commensurately-first (katholou proton) demonstration (Friedlein 75–76, 178–183, 206, 381–383).

aristotle:met:981b-1078a.author: Aristotle
aristotle:met:981b-1078a.note: Egyptian leisure of the priestly caste (64–65), Protagoras's critique of geometric tangency (139–140), intelligible matter (hyle noete, 48–53), and mathematical beauty (26–27).

aristotle:de-anima:III.4-8.author: Aristotle
aristotle:de-anima:III.4-8.note: Motion of a point generating a line (97), soul as 'place of forms' (topos eidon, 16), and passive intellect / phantasia (51–52).

aristotle:de-caelo:I.5.author: Aristotle
aristotle:de-caelo:I.5.note: Lemma invoked by Proclus (Friedlein 371, 10) in his attempted proof of Postulate 5: two straight lines diverging from one point separate beyond any finite distance.

euclid:elements.author: Euclid
euclid:elements.note: The canonical treatise expounded throughout Proclus's Commentary; cross-linked via GEOMETOR `:just:` to `geometor/euclid` and `geometor/elements`.

eudemus:history-of-geometry.author: Eudemus of Rhodes
eudemus:history-of-geometry.note: Lost Peripatetic history of Greek geometry whose priceless fragments—the Eudemian Summary and attributions to Thales, Oenopides, Hippocrates, and the Pythagoreans—survive almost solely through Proclus.

geminus:philokalia.author: Geminus of Rhodes
geminus:philokalia.work: Theory of the Mathematical Sciences / Philokalia (fragments)
geminus:philokalia.note: Encyclopedic Stoic-mathematical treatise on the classification of sciences, curves (homoeomeric, spiric, cissoid, conchoid), asymptotic lines, and postulates.

ptolemy:parallel-lines.author: Claudius Ptolemy
ptolemy:parallel-lines.work: That Straight Lines Produced from Angles Less Than Two Right Angles Meet (fragments)
ptolemy:parallel-lines.note: Lost monograph attempting to demonstrate Euclid's Fifth Postulate; preserved solely in Proclus's Commentary on Prop. I.29.

pappus:collectio.author: Pappus of Alexandria
pappus:collectio.note: Source of the famous zero-construction symmetry proof of Prop. I.5 (pons asinorum) and critical notes on Postulate 4 and the Common Notions.

heath:1926.author: Sir Thomas Little Heath
heath:1926.work: The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements (2nd ed., 3 vols.)
heath:1926.note: Primary modern critical commentary on Euclid in `geometor/euclid`, citing Proclus across 156 distinct Friedlein loci.

hoenen:1954.author: Petrus H. J. Hoenen, S.J.
hoenen:1954.work: De Noetica Geometriae: Origine Theoriae Cognitionis
hoenen:1954.note: Companion GEOMETOR treatise engaging Proclus on sensible inexactitude, phantasia and intelligible matter (Friedlein 12, 49, 97, 139–140, 185), and the epistemology of Postulate 5 (Friedlein 191, 365–373).
